claim: Main stress is overwhelmingly predictable from moraic structure: it falls on the penultimate mora, with only a very small set of lexical exceptions.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The grammar explicitly notes a small number of exceptions, so the rule is staged as near-categorical rather than exceptionless.

claim: Rising and falling glide-vowel sequences differ prosodically: final rising sequences do not attract final stress because the glide patterns as an onset, whereas a final falling diphthong forms a bimoraic rhyme and is stressed.

source_forms.rising: CV.(C)GV#; G patterns as onset and sequence does not make final syllable heavy
source_forms.falling: CV.CVG#; VG is a bimoraic complex rhyme and final syllable receives stress

normalized_environment: rising GV = onset+V (light); falling VG = 2μ rhyme (heavy)
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The contrast is structural: it does not claim all orthographic or phonetic vowel-glide sequences are equivalent.
table_figure: examples contrasting rising and falling diphthongs

claim: Vowels that become nasal through spreading remain light for stress: a final derived nasal vowel does not attract final stress as a phonemic long/heavy nucleus would.

source_forms.stress: final nasalized V is not an independent stress attractor

exceptions_or_counterexamples: This concerns nasalization created by spreading and should not be generalized to unrelated sources of vowel weight.

claim: Nasal spreading is optional and directionally asymmetric: regressive spreading is chiefly triggered by a nasal vowel, whereas progressive spreading can be triggered by a nasal onset or nasal vowel.

source_forms.regressive: nasal V mainly spreads left to vowels/glides
source_forms.progressive: nasal onset C or nasal V can spread right

formal_environment: nasal segment adjacent to eligible targets
normalized_environment: [nasal] spreads optionally left/right with trigger-specific directionality
scope: word-internal phonology, with an external-sandhi extension recorded separately
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Not every intervening segment is a target: segment classes differ in transparency/blocking, and spreading is optional.

claim: Nasal spreading targets vowels and glides and can target the rhotic [ɾ]; /h/ is transparent, while other consonants—including /l/—block spreading.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The rhotic and glides are optional targets in some trigger configurations; the class membership therefore does not imply obligatory nasalization on every occurrence.

claim: Regressive nasal spreading can apply postlexically across a word boundary, optionally nasalizing material in the final syllable of the preceding word.
normalized_environment: nasal feature may spread left across # into immediately preceding final syllable
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The process is optional and locally bounded in the examples; it is not described as unrestricted phrase-wide harmony.

claim: The vowel of the detransitivizing/reflexive-reciprocal prefix shows limited harmony with the initial vowel of the verb: /əd-/ surfaces with /o/- or /a/-quality before corresponding stem-initial vowels, while no analogous change occurs before /ɨ, ə/.

source_forms.note: additional consonantal alternations occur before e/i

normalized_environment: prefix V copies/approaches stem-initial vowel quality in a limited subset {o,a}
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The alternation is not general word-wide vowel harmony: /ɨ, ə/ do not trigger the same vowel change, and e/i contexts involve separate consonantal alternations.

claim: The possessum suffix /-rɨ/ has a restricted back-vowel harmony allomorph /-ru/ after stems ending in /o/ or /u/, while /-rɨ/ occurs elsewhere.
normalized_environment: ɨ -> u / {o,u}]Stem r__ in possessum suffix
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The rule is suffix-specific and therefore not evidence for unrestricted lexical vowel harmony.

claim: Fast speech commonly deletes the initial vowel of disyllabic function words, and a noninitial vowel may also delete in the animate demonstrative /awəkə/.

source_forms.initial_deletion: initial V of disyllabic function words commonly lost in fast speech; examples include əmə

formal_environment: # V C V in high-frequency function words; V in awəkə
normalized_environment: unstressed/function-word V -> Ø in fast speech, lexically/domain conditioned
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The grammar describes common/possible fast-speech variants, not obligatory deletion in careful speech or across all lexical classes.

claim: Intervocalic /h/ can delete between identical back vowels, yielding either a two-syllable VhV realization or a long vowel; the deletion occurs in both dialects but is especially common in Western Bakairi and frequently involves the nominalizing suffix.
normalized_environment: h -> Ø / V_back __ V_back when flanking vowels identical; coalescence -> Vː
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Both retained-[h] and deletion/coalescence outputs occur; this is variation rather than categorical loss.

claim: Portuguese loans are stratified by degree of integration: older loans tend to be adapted to Bakairi phonotactics, while recent loans can retain Portuguese-like structures that violate native restrictions.

explicit_native_constraints_violated: normally no more than one word-internal voiceless obstruent

normalized_environment: loan integration correlates with age/degree of nativization; recent loans license marginal structures
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Recent borrowings are explicitly allowed to violate patterns that are robust in native vocabulary, so loan tokens must not be used as simple counterevidence to the native constraints.

claim: Integrated Portuguese loans show active native repairs including coda deletion, stress reassignment, and morphologically conditioned changes in stop voicing; these repairs need not apply to the newest loans.

repairs: native affixation can alter stop voicing
source_forms.examples: carteira and papel adaptations discussed in §2.7

normalized_environment: loan repair satisfies native coda/voicing/prosodic restrictions, variably by loan stratum
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Recent loans may remain comparatively unadapted and therefore do not obligatorily undergo all repairs.
